p1.linkedin:
A pattern we see often when we look at doctors' online presence: the care in the clinic is excellent, and the Instagram account went quiet months ago.

Patients notice. Before they book, they look you up, check your profile, your photos and what other patients wrote, and they decide in a few seconds whether to trust you. A quiet account or a missing phone number sends them to the next name on the list.

Aloui Med Digital Bridge (AMDB) exists to close that gap between the quality of the care and the quality of the online presence. We build and run the digital side for doctors, clinics and labs, in Arabic and English, so their reputation online matches the one they've earned in practice.

If you run a practice and want a second opinion on what patients see when they search for you, get in touch.

p2.linkedin:
Three patterns we keep finding when we review clinic Instagram accounts. Each one costs appointments, and each one is easy to fix.

1. The last post is months old. A patient sees that and wonders whether the clinic is still open.
2. There is no obvious way to book. If the number takes effort to find, the patient books with someone else.
3. The visuals undersell the practice. Excellent medicine shown through blurry phone photos sends the wrong signal.

The full breakdown is in the document above, in English and Arabic.

If your practice's account has one of these, we're happy to look at it with you.
